title: DCGM — Profiling
book_use: Chapters 1 and 20: distinguishes SM activity, occupancy, tensor-pipe activity, DRAM activity, and other profiling counters; supports the warning that one utilization percentage cannot diagnose end-to-end useful work.

title: DCGM Exporter Metrics
book_use: Chapters 1 and 20: inventory of device, power, memory, PCIe, NVLink, utilization, and profiling metrics used to connect accelerator behavior to system bottlenecks.

title: Multi-Instance GPU User Guide — Introduction
book_use: Chapters 1, 10, and 19: evidence that a physical GPU can be partitioned into isolated instances to improve sharing and quality of service; partitioning remains workload-dependent.

title: MLPerf Inference — Submission Guide
book_use: Chapter 2: MLPerf defines separate Datacenter Offline, Server, and Interactive scenarios, illustrating that throughput and latency are different operating objectives rather than one universal performance number.

title: MLPerf Inference Datacenter
book_use: Chapter 2: current datacenter inference benchmark context; use benchmark results only within their specified models, quality targets, scenarios, and hardware configurations.

title: NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU
book_use: Chapters 3 and 15: hardware context for HBM capacity, memory bandwidth, accelerator power, and peak arithmetic capability; peak specifications are not sustained application performance.

author_or_institution: Tri Dao; Daniel Y. Fu; Stefano Ermon; Atri Rudra; Christopher Ré
title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
book_use: Chapter 3: demonstrates that reducing reads and writes between GPU memory levels can materially improve transformer wall-clock performance without changing the exact attention result.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
book_use: Chapters 3 and 4: documents KV-cache fragmentation and duplication as serving bottlenecks and reports 2–4x throughput gains for vLLM in the paper's evaluated settings; do not generalize the multiplier.

title: CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide
book_use: Chapters 3 and 11: supports the practical importance of coalesced memory access, minimizing host-device transfers, and overlapping data movement with computation where applicable.

title: TensorRT-LLM — KV Cache System
book_use: Chapters 3, 5, and 8: describes block-based KV-cache management, reuse, offload, and eviction; shows that cache policy is part of serving capacity.

title: vLLM Documentation
book_use: Chapters 4, 5, 7, 8, and 17: current serving features include PagedAttention, continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching, quantization, speculative decoding, and distributed inference.

title: TensorRT-LLM — Attention
book_use: Chapter 4: documents in-flight batching and packed request handling as techniques for combining context and generation work while reducing padding waste.

title: TensorRT-LLM — Tuning Max Batch Size and Max Num Tokens
book_use: Chapter 4: shows that batch and token scheduler limits are explicit performance knobs and that optimal values depend on workload and hardware.

title: Automatic Prefix Caching
book_use: Chapters 5 and 8: explains reuse of KV-cache blocks for repeated prefixes to avoid redundant prompt computation; benefit depends on prefix reuse in the workload.

title: TensorRT-LLM — Memory Usage of TensorRT-LLM
book_use: Chapter 5: documents how runtime memory includes model and KV-cache allocations and how context length, batch size, and generated tokens affect serving memory requirements.

title: Megatron Core — Context Parallelism
book_use: Chapters 5 and 12: explains context parallelism as a method for distributing long-sequence activations and the communication tradeoffs that accompany it.

title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
book_use: Chapter 6: demonstrates learned routing between stronger and weaker models and reports more than 2x cost reduction in some benchmark settings without response-quality loss; production transfer is not guaranteed.

author_or_institution: Lingjiao Chen; Matei Zaharia; James Zou
title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
book_use: Chapter 6: evaluates model cascades, prompt adaptation, and approximation for cost-aware LLM use; reported savings are benchmark-specific and should not be treated as universal production economics.

title: TensorRT-LLM — Quantization
book_use: Chapters 6 and 7: documents supported lower-precision formats and quantization techniques that can reduce model footprint or compute cost, subject to model-specific quality and hardware effects.

title: NCCL — Overview
book_use: Chapters 11 and 12: collective communication primitives and topology-aware communication are central to multi-GPU work; distributed efficiency depends on communication as well as accelerator arithmetic.

title: Megatron Core — Parallelism Strategies Guide
book_use: Chapters 11, 12, and 16: documents data, tensor, pipeline, context, expert, and sharded parallelism and their communication and memory tradeoffs.

title: Megatron Core — Data Loading at Scale
book_use: Chapter 13: documents data-pipeline startup barriers, simultaneous index access, cache preparation, and large-scale data-loading practices; supports the claim that upstream data stages can leave many accelerators idle even when raw bandwidth is not the only bottleneck.

title: Megatron Core — Distributed Checkpointing
book_use: Chapter 14: documents distributed checkpoint save/load, resharding choices, and asynchronous checkpoint saving; supports the trade between pause time, I/O, recovery flexibility, and checkpoint complexity.

title: NVIDIA System Management Interface
book_use: Chapter 15: documents board and module power readings, software power caps, enforced power limits, performance-state effects, and power smoothing; supports treating power as an explicit operating constraint rather than a post-hoc utility bill.

title: Domain Power Service — Power Policies
book_use: Chapter 15: documents node- and GPU-level power policies across datacenter topology, supporting the claim that fleet-level power management can be a scheduling and capacity concern.

title: Megatron Core — Advanced Features
book_use: Chapter 16: documents model-system features including Mixture of Experts, multiple parallelism axes, FP8 training, model families, offload, and data loading; use as evidence that architecture choices change communication, memory, and runtime requirements.

title: Speculative Decoding
book_use: Chapter 17: documents multiple speculative-decoding methods and explicitly scopes benefits by workload, including medium-to-low-QPS memory-bound serving; supports the chapter's conditional rather than universal treatment of speculation.

title: Prepare for Amazon EC2 Spot Instance interruptions
book_use: Chapter 18: spot capacity can be interrupted and applications must be interruption-tolerant; low sticker price is not completed-job cost by itself.

title: Dynamic Workload Scheduler
book_use: Chapters 18 and 19: flex-start and calendar-style scheduling illustrate the economic value of matching non-urgent AI jobs to capacity availability.

title: Schedule GPUs
book_use: Chapters 10 and 19: Kubernetes exposes GPUs through device plugins and resource requests, useful context for why accelerator scheduling often begins with coarse, non-shareable resource units unless additional partitioning is used.

title: The Tail at Scale
book_use: Chapters 20, 21, and 23: documents how tail latency is amplified in large fan-out systems and discusses hedged requests as a deliberate trade of modest extra work for lower latency variability; the paper's quantitative examples are historical and workload-specific.
